Note::strip_bom¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::strip_bom() const

Remove A Leading Byte-Order Mark From Every Cell¶

strip_bom() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with a UTF-8 byte-order mark (U+FEFF, the bytes EF BB BF) removed from the start of each cell that begins with one. A BOM commonly sneaks in when reading files exported by editors or spreadsheets; left in place it breaks a leading-token check, a numeric parse, or an exact-match lookup on the first field.

Only a BOM at position 0 is removed. A U+FEFF elsewhere in the cell is left alone — that is a zero-width no-break space, and strip_zero_width is the method that removes those wherever they occur.

strip_bom is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. A cell without a leading BOM is unchanged.

Example 1: A Batch¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note(
    {std::string("\xEF\xBB\xBF") + "hello", "plain",
     std::string("mid") + "\xEF\xBB\xBF" + "bom"}).strip_bom();
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["hello", "plain", "mid﻿bom"]

The leading BOM is gone from the first cell; the mid-cell U+FEFF in the third is kept.

See Also¶

  • Note::strip_zero_width: remove U+FEFF and other zero-width characters anywhere in the cell.

  • Note::strip: trim whitespace from the boundary.

  • Note::remove_prefix: remove a known literal prefix.
